title: How diseases spread: epidemics and pandemics
examples: What is the difference between an epidemic and a pandemic?
How does the R number help us understand how fast a sickness spreads?
What are the main ways diseases can travel from person to person?

explain.say: Today we are learning how sicknesses travel from person to person. This process is called transmission.

draw.text: How diseases spread: epidemics and pandemics

explain.say: An infection chain shows the path a germ takes. It needs a source, a path, and a new host.
The R number tells us how many people one sick person infects. It is called the basic reproduction number.

draw.text: R number: New cases per case

explain.say: An outbreak is when a sickness spreads quickly in one small area. It is a sudden increase in cases.
A pandemic is when a sickness spreads across many different countries. It affects the whole world.
In real life, think about a school cold outbreak. If everyone gets it, the R number is high. Washing hands lowers the R number.

faq.q: What is the difference between an epidemic and a pandemic?
faq.a: An epidemic is a sudden increase in cases within a specific community or region. A pandemic means the disease has spread across multiple continents or worldwide.
asks: When is an outbreak considered a pandemic?
Does an epidemic always become a pandemic?

faq.q: What does the R number actually measure?
faq.a: The R number measures the average number of people one infected person will pass the sickness to. If this number is less than one, the sickness will start to decline.
asks: How do we know if a disease is spreading?
Is R greater than one bad?

faq.q: Are there different ways diseases can spread?
faq.a: Yes, diseases can spread through direct contact, through contaminated air droplets, or via contaminated objects or water.
asks: Can germs spread through the air?
What is a common way germs travel?

faq.q: How do we stop a disease from becoming a pandemic?
faq.a: We can reduce the R number by improving hygiene, using masks, and vaccinating people to build immunity.
asks: What is the best way to stop a global spread?

faq.q: What is the difference between an outbreak and a local spread?
faq.a: An outbreak is a sharp, noticeable spike in cases in a limited area. A local spread is just the normal, expected rate of cases in a small area.

facts: Diseases spread through various routes like air, water, and direct contact.
An R number below one means the spread of the disease is slowing down.
An outbreak is a rapid increase in cases in a specific, limited area.
A pandemic signifies worldwide spread of a disease, affecting many countries.

quiz.say: If the R number drops below one, what happens to the sickness?

options.show: The sickness will become a pandemic.
options.say: The sickness will become a pandemic.

options.show: The R number must become zero.
options.say: The R number must become zero.

options.show: The sickness will start to decline.
options.say: The sickness will start to decline.

quiz.why: When R is less than one, each sick person infects less than one new person, causing the chain to break.

wrong.0: A low R number suggests containment, not global spread.
wrong.1: Zero is very hard to achieve; 'declining' is the correct general term.
wrong.3: This is too strong; it might slow down but not stop instantly.

quiz.say: A sickness spreading across all continents is called a:
quiz.why: Pandemic specifically describes the worldwide scale of the outbreak.

wrong.0: An epidemic is usually large, but not necessarily global in scope.
wrong.2: An outbreak is limited to a smaller, local area.
wrong.3: Transmission is the method of spread, not the name of the event.

quiz.say: If a single sick person infects exactly three other people, what is the R number?
quiz.why: The R number is the average number of people one case infects.

wrong.0: This is not a number; it describes the action, not the rate.
wrong.1: While related, the R number is a rate, not a count of people.
wrong.3: This would mean the person infects less than one person.
